g.L10.loc.title: Locative -DA: in / at / on
g.L10.loc.reference:
**-DA** means *in*, *at* or *on*: **ev·de** "at home", **masa·da** "on the table", **çanta·da** "in the bag".

**Vowel (A):** look at the *last* vowel of the word.
a ı o u → **-da** · e i ö ü → **-de**

**Consonant (D):** after one of the voiceless consonants **f s t k ç ş h p** ("**F**ı**st**ı**kç**ı **Ş**a**h**a**p**") → **-ta / -te**; otherwise **-da / -de**.

The word itself never changes before -DA: *kitap → kitapta*, *mutfak → mutfakta*.
After a plural: **ev·ler·de** "in the houses".

First and last vowels differ in harmony: only the last one counts

g.L11.loc_copula.title: Location + 'to be'; apostrophes on names
g.L11.loc_copula.reference:
To say *I am at home*, put the "to be" endings from L5 **after** -DA:

| Pronoun | Form | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ben | ev·de·**yim** | I am at home |
| sen | ev·de·**sin** | you are at home |
| o | ev·de | he / she is at home |
| biz | ev·de·**yiz** | we are at home |
| siz | ev·de·**siniz** | you (pl. / polite) are at home |
| onlar | ev·de(·**ler**) | they are at home |

**Buffer y:** -DA always ends in a vowel, so *-(y)Im* and *-(y)Iz* always get their **y**: ev·de·**y**im, park·ta·**y**ız.

**Harmony:** the person ending looks at the vowel of -DA. **-da** → -yım, -sın, -yız, -sınız, -lar · **-de** → -yim, -sin, -yiz, -siniz, -ler.

**Questions and negation** work as in L6–L7: *Evde misin?* "Are you at home?" · *Evde değilim.* "I'm not at home."

**Names take an apostrophe** before any ending: *İstanbul'da*, *Ankara'dayım*, *Ali'de* "at Ali's". The ending follows the usual rules: *Ahmet'te* (t after t).

*Neredesin?* "Where are you?" = nere·de·sin.

g.L12.abl.title: Ablative -DAn: from
g.L12.abl.reference:
**-DAn** means *from*: **ev·den** "from home", **okul·dan** "from school", **İstanbul'dan** "from Istanbul".

It is the locative **-DA** plus **n**, so the same two questions decide its form:

- **Vowel (A):** last vowel a ı o u → **-dan** · e i ö ü → **-den**
- **Consonant (D):** after **f s t k ç ş h p** ("Fıstıkçı Şahap") → **-tan / -ten**; otherwise **-dan / -den**.

The word itself doesn't change: *kitap → kitaptan*, *sokak → sokaktan*. Exception: a compound like *yatak odası* adds **n**, as with -DA: *yatak odası·n·dan*. After a plural: **ev·ler·den**.

**With "to be" endings** (L11), no verb is needed: *Neredensin?* "Where are you from?" — *Londra'danım.* "I'm from London." -DAn ends in a consonant, so there is **no buffer y**: Londra'dan·**ım**, İzmir'den·**iz**.

*Nerelisin?* (the L5 phrase) is the more standard way to ask where someone is from; *Neredensin?* is fine in conversation.

⚠️ Don't mix them up: *Londra'dayım* "I'm **in** London" · *Londra'danım* "I'm **from** London".

Names keep their apostrophe: *Türkiye'den*, *Ahmet'ten*.

g.L13.clitic_de.title: Clitic de/da 'too' vs locative -DA; ve, ama
g.L13.clitic_de.reference:
**de / da** = *too, also*. It is a **separate word**, placed right after the word it adds to:

*Ben de.* "Me too." · *Ayşe de evde.* "Ayşe is at home **too**." · *Kitap da çantada.* "The book is in the bag **too**."

- **Vowel:** a/e harmony with the word before: a ı o u → **da**, e i ö ü → **de**.
- **Consonant:** it **never** becomes *te / ta*: *Ahmet **de***, *kitap **da***, *tavuk **da*** (not ~~Ahmet te~~, ~~kitap ta~~).

**Separate or attached?** The locative **-DA** is *attached* and does change d → t: *kitap**ta*** "in the book", *Ahmet'**te*** "at Ahmet's". Test: leave the word out. If the sentence still makes sense, it was the clitic: *Ahmet ~~de~~ parkta* → *Ahmet parkta*. ✓

Both together: *Ev**de** **de** kedi var.* "There's a cat at home **too**."

The clitic never takes an apostrophe. Watch these pairs: *Ali de* "Ali too" / *Ali'de* "at Ali's"; *ben de* "me too" / *bende* "with me, I have it".

**ve** = *and* joins words: *Ali ve Ayşe evde.*
**ama** = *but* joins two statements: *Ali evde ama Ayşe okulda.*

patterns.description: de after e i ö ü, da after a ı o u
The clitic never becomes te / ta (Ahmet de, kitap da)
Separate 'too' vs attached locative (Ahmet de / Ahmet'te)

L10.title: Locative -DA: in / at / on
not_yet: personal endings on the location (evdeyim) → L11

cards.body:
🐈 **Kedi nerede?** "Where is the cat?"
🛋️ **Kedi kanepede.** "The cat is on the sofa."

Turkish doesn't say *on the sofa*. It adds an ending to the word: **kanepe → kanepe·de**.

cards.title: Meaning: in, at, on
cards.body:
**-DA = in, at, on**. One ending covers all three English prepositions.

| Turkish | English |
|---|---|
| ev·**de** | **at** home / **in** the house |
| masa·**da** | **on** the table |
| çanta·**da** | **in** the bag |

💡 There's no "is" in *Kedi kanepede*. As in L3, the 3rd person needs no verb "to be".

cards.title: The vowel: a or e?
cards.body:
The **A** in -DA follows 2-way harmony. Look at the **last vowel** of the word:

| Last vowel | Ending | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a ı o u (back) | **-da** | oda·da, okul·da, banyo·da |
| e i ö ü (front) | **-de** | ev·de, bahçe·de, pencere·de |

⚠️ Only the **last** vowel counts: o·to·**bü**s → front → otobüs·**te** (not ~~otobüsta~~).

cards.title: The consonant: d or t?
cards.body:
The **D** in -DA becomes **t** after a *voiceless* consonant. There are only 8 of them:

**F**ı**st**ı**kç**ı **Ş**a**h**a**p** — "Şahap the pistachio seller" → **f s t k ç ş h p**

| Word ends in… | Ending | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| a vowel | -da / -de | masa·da, kanepe·de |
| another consonant | -da / -de | okul·da, ev·de |
| f s t k ç ş h p | **-ta / -te** | kitap·**ta**, mutfak·**ta**, süt·**te**, otobüs·**te** |

✅ -DA starts with a consonant, so **the word itself never changes**: *kitap → kitapta*.

cards.title: Step by step
cards.body:
Two questions, every time: **which vowel?** then **which consonant?**

Plural first, then the location: **ev·ler·de** "in the houses".

cards.title: Where?
cards.body:
**Nerede?** "Where?" — *Kitap nerede? — Kitap çantada.*
**burada** "here" · **orada** "there" (they already contain -da: bura·da, ora·da)

items.note: Trap: first vowel o is back, last vowel ü is front.

feedback.ev·de·ler: The plural comes first, then the location: **ev·ler·de**.

L11.title: Location + 'to be'; apostrophes
not_yet: the separate word de 'too' (Ben de evdeyim) → L13

cards.body:
📱 **Neredesin?** "Where are you?"
🏠 **Evdeyim.** "I'm at home."

One word, three pieces: **ev·de·yim** = home · at · I am.

cards.title: Location + person
cards.body:
You already know both pieces: **-DA** "at" (L10) and the "to be" endings (L5). Put them in that order: **place · -DA · person**.

| | okul "school" | ev "home" |
|---|---|---|
| ben | okul·da·**yım** | ev·de·**yim** |
| sen | okul·da·**sın** | ev·de·**sin** |
| o | okul·da | ev·de |
| biz | okul·da·**yız** | ev·de·**yiz** |
| siz | okul·da·**sınız** | ev·de·**siniz** |
| onlar | okul·da(·**lar**) | ev·de(·**ler**) |

💡 The pronoun is optional: *Okuldayım* already says "I".

cards.title: Two small rules
cards.body:
**1. Buffer y.** -DA always ends in a vowel, so -(y)Im and -(y)Iz always take **y**: ev·de·**y**im, park·ta·**y**ız.

**2. Harmony keeps going.** The person ending looks at the vowel of -DA:

| -DA gave… | then |
|---|---|
| **-da / -ta** | -yım, -sın, -yız, -sınız, -lar |
| **-de / -te** | -yim, -sin, -yiz, -siniz, -ler |

*park → park·ta → park·ta·yız* · *market → market·te → market·te·yim*

cards.title: Questions and 'not'
cards.body:
Same as L6–L7: the person ending moves onto **mI** or **değil**.

*Parkta mısın?* "Are you in the park?" — *Evet, parktayım.* / *Hayır, parkta değilim.*

They: *-lAr* stays on the word: *Evdeler mi?* (But with *onlar*, people usually just say *Onlar evde*.)

🔊 Stress falls just **before** the person ending: ev**DE**yim, park**TA**yız.

cards.title: Names take an apostrophe
cards.body:
Names of people and places keep their spelling, so an **apostrophe** separates the ending:

*İstanbul'**da*** "in Istanbul" · *Ankara'**dayım*** "I'm in Ankara" · *Ali'**de*** "at Ali's"

The ending follows the usual rules, based on how the name **sounds**: *Ahmet'**te*** (t after t), *İzmir'**deyim***, *Paris'**te***.

Only **names** get the apostrophe. Language names don't: *Türkçe**de***, not ~~Türkçe'de~~.

🔊 Stress stays on the name: **İS**tanbul'da, **AN**kara'dayım.

cards.title: Step by step
cards.body:
Three questions, in order: **which place?** → **-da or -de, d or t?** → **which person?**

- *we · park* → park·**ta** → park·ta·**yız**
- *you · hospital* → hastane·**de** → hastane·de·**sin**
- *I · Ankara* → Ankara·**'da** → Ankara'da·**yım**

feedback.evdesın: -de has a front vowel, so the person ending is **-sin**: evdesin.

feedback.okuldasin: -da has a back vowel, so the person ending is **-sın**: okuldasın.

feedback.parkdayız: **park** ends in **k**, one of the Fıstıkçı Şahap letters → **t**: parktayız.
feedback.parktaız: -ta ends in a vowel, so -(y)Iz needs the buffer **y**: parktayız.
feedback.parktayiz: -ta has a back vowel, so the person ending is **-yız**: parktayız.

items.prompt: you (plural / polite) are at the hospital

items.note: With onlar, -lAr is usually left out; bahçedeler is correct but less common.

feedback.İstanbuldayım: **İstanbul** is a name, so it takes an apostrophe before the ending: **İstanbul'dayım**.

feedback.parktayiz: -ta has a back vowel, so the person ending is **-yız**: parktayız.

L12.title: Ablative -DAn: from
not_yet: verbs that take the ablative (korkmak) → preview only, produced from L17
the separate word de 'too' (Ben de İstanbul'danım) → L13

cards.body:
🌍 **Neredensin?** "Where are you from?"
🇬🇧 **Londra'danım.** "I'm from London."

*From* is one more ending: **Londra'·dan·ım** = London · from · I am.

cards.title: -DAn = -DA + n
cards.body:
You already know the hard part. **-DAn** is the locative plus **n**, with the same two choices:

| Word ends in… | in / at (L10) | from |
|---|---|---|
| back vowel a ı o u | okul·da | okul·**dan** |
| front vowel e i ö ü | ev·de | ev·**den** |
| f s t k ç ş h p | kitap·ta, otobüs·te | kitap·**tan**, otobüs·**ten** |

✅ The word doesn't change: *sokak → sokaktan*. Names keep the apostrophe: *İstanbul'dan*, *Türkiye'den*, *Paris'ten*.

cards.title: Where are you from?
cards.body:
Add the "to be" endings, exactly as in L11:

| | |
|---|---|
| ben | Londra'dan·**ım** |
| sen | Londra'dan·**sın** |
| o | Londra'dan |
| biz | Londra'dan·**ız** |
| siz | Londra'dan·**sınız** |

-DAn ends in **n**, a consonant, so there's **no buffer y**: Londra'dan**ım**, İzmir'den**iz** (not ~~Londra'danyım~~).

**Nereden?** "Where from?" = nere·den. *Neredensin?* "Where are you from?"

💬 *Nerelisin?* (from L5) is the more standard way to ask; *Neredensin?* is fine in conversation.

cards.title: in or from?
cards.body:
One letter changes the meaning. Listen for the **n**:

- *Londra'**da**yım* "I'm **in** London"
- *Londra'**dan**ım* "I'm **from** London"

cards.title: Preview: verbs that want 'from'
cards.body:
Some verbs take -DAn where English uses another preposition. You'll use them once verbs arrive (L17); just notice them for now:

- **korkmak** "to be afraid **of**": *kedi**den** korkmak* "to be afraid of cats"
- **hoşlanmak** "to like": *çay**dan** hoşlanmak* "to like tea"

feedback.Londradanım: **Londra** is a name, so it takes an apostrophe before the ending: **Londra'danım**.

items.note: Ear training for the n of -DAn.
Trap: first vowel o is back, last vowel ü is front.

feedback.ev·den·ler: The plural comes first, then the case: **ev·ler·den**.

feedback.Londradanım: **Londra** is a name, so it takes an apostrophe before the ending: **Londra'danım**.

L13.title: Clitic de/da vs locative; ve, ama
not_yet: de/da with verbs (Ahmet de geliyor) → L15
the question form with de (Sen de mi?) → later review

cards.body:
🙋 **Ben okuldayım.** "I'm at school."
🙋‍♀️ **Ben de!** "Me too!"

This **de** is not the ending from L10. It's a separate little word meaning **too**.

cards.title: de / da = too, also
cards.body:
Put it **right after** the word it adds to, as a **separate word**:

| Turkish | English |
|---|---|
| Ayşe **de** evde. | Ayşe is at home **too**. |
| Kitap **da** çantada. | The book is in the bag **too**. |
| Biz **de** parktayız. | We're in the park **too**. |

**Vowel:** a/e harmony with the word before: a ı o u → **da**, e i ö ü → **de**.

cards.title: It never becomes te / ta
cards.body:
Fıstıkçı Şahap does **not** apply to the clitic. It stays **d**:

✅ Ahmet **de** · kitap **da** · tavuk **da**
❌ ~~Ahmet te~~ · ~~kitap ta~~ · ~~tavuk ta~~

The locative, attached to the word, *does* change: kitap**ta** "in the book", Ahmet'**te** "at Ahmet's".

cards.title: Attached or separate?
cards.body:
**Test:** leave the *de / da* out. If the sentence still makes sense, it was "too", so write it **separately**.

- *Ahmet ~~de~~ parkta.* → *Ahmet parkta.* ✓ → **Ahmet de** (too)
- *Kedi bahçe ~~de~~.* → *Kedi bahçe.* ✗ → **bahçede** (in the garden)

Both at once: *Ev**de** **de** kedi var.* "There's a cat at home **too**."

⚠️ Two pairs that even native speakers mix up in writing:

| too (separate) | location (attached) |
|---|---|
| **Ali de.** "Ali too." | **Ali'de.** "At Ali's." / "Ali has it." |
| **Ben de.** "Me too." | **Bende.** "With me." / "I have it." |

The clitic never takes an apostrophe: *Ali de*, not ~~Ali'de~~ for "Ali too".

cards.title: ve and ama
cards.body:
**ve** "and" joins words: *Ali **ve** Ayşe evde.* "Ali and Ayşe are at home."
**ama** "but" joins two statements: *Ali evde **ama** Ayşe okulda.*

items.prompt: Ahmet is in the park too.

items.note: kitap ends in p, but the clitic never becomes ta.

options: Ali and Ayşe are at home.
Ali is at home but Ayşe isn't.
items.answer: Ali and Ayşe are at home.

feedback.te: **de / da** 'too' never changes to **t**, even after Fıstıkçı Şahap: **Ahmet de**.
feedback.da: **de / da** follows the last vowel of **Ahmet** (e): **Ahmet de**.

feedback.ta: **de / da** 'too' never changes to **t**, even after Fıstıkçı Şahap: **Tavuk da**.
feedback.de: **de / da** follows the last vowel of **tavuk** (u): **Tavuk da**.

feedback.bahçe de: Here it means *in the garden*: the location ending is **attached**: **bahçede**.

items.note: Ali de (too) vs Ali'de (at Ali's): the clitic never takes an apostrophe.
